    - heading "Accessibility" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: A group named by its title; the rolling number is aria-hidden and screen readers get the final "used of limit" in one sentence
      - listitem: The field of cells is decorative – every number it shows is in the list below
      - listitem: Parts with items are buttons with aria-expanded; closed lists are inert, remove buttons are named after their item
      - listitem: "The caption in the last row is announced politely: compacting, how much was saved, and how much is left once the window fills up"
    - heading "Motion" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: Any change sweeps through the field cell by cell, so removing a file empties its cells from left to right and everything behind it moves up
      - listitem: Compacting makes the part's cells shimmer in a lighter wave while the caption shimmers "Compacting…"; then most of them clear, the numbers roll down and the button morphs into a green check on a light green fill with "Compacted" for a moment and then fades away – it only comes back once the part has grown again
      - listitem: Hovering a part (row or cells) fades the other cells and rolls the big number to that part
      - listitem: Items unfold in place; a removed item folds away before it goes
      - listitem: With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement
    - heading "Responsive behavior" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: Fills its container up to 360px. Below 310px the field puts fewer cells in a row so they stay readable, the model tag shortens and Compact keeps only its icon
      - listitem: "Touch screens: taller rows and buttons"
      - listitem: "Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme=\"dark\""
    - heading "Notes for AI" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Give your coding assistant this summary instead of screenshots.
    - list:
      - listitem: A part with items takes its tokens from the items' sum – leave tokens out there
      - listitem: One cell stands for limit / cells tokens; any part with tokens gets at least one cell so it never disappears
      - listitem: The card does not count tokens – pass the numbers your provider or tokenizer returns
